references.title: The Movie Book
references.subtitle: Danny Leigh, Louis Baxter, Kieran Grant, John Farndon, Damon Wise (Contributors)
references.description: Did Chinatown really subvert the noir genre? What are the effects of Pulp Fiction's fragmented screenplay? How do multiple points of view affect the notion of reality in Rashomon? By showcasing the best films of all time, this book answers these questions and many others while offering an overview of the world of cinema. Written in plain language and packed with iconic images from the films, as well as posters and infographics, The Movie Book explores the characters, directors, screenplays and key themes of more than a hundred of the greatest films ever made. Whether you're a die-hard film buff or an occasional moviegoer looking for recommendations, this book will give you new perspectives on your favorite films or an introduction to a great many other gems you can't miss.

references.title: Cinema: The Whole Story
references.subtitle: Philip Kemp (Author)
references.description: If you love cinema and want to learn more about the seventh art, this book is a must for your library. Organized chronologically and written by an experienced team of specialist critics, this is a stimulating guide to the history of cinema, enhanced with in-depth analyses of masterpieces and illustrated with images of unforgettable scenes.

references.title: 1001 Movies You Must See Before You Die
references.subtitle: Steven Jay Schneider, Ian Haydn Smith (Editors)
references.description: Translated into 25 languages and with more than one million copies sold, 1001 Movies You Must See Before You Die includes works from more than 30 countries and reveals the very best of cinema of all time. In this updated edition, which features recent hits, more than 50 renowned critics selected 1001 must-see films and gathered them in this reference guide for everyone passionate about the seventh art.

image.content_description: Cover of the book 1001 Movies You Must See Before You Die

references.title: The Story of Film
references.subtitle: Mark Cousins (Author)
references.description: From silent film, through the ingenuity of sound cinema, to the incredible innovations of the digital era, Mark Cousins presents a complete and accessible overview of the history of world cinema. It unveils the techniques, aspirations and inventions of each era, in different countries and by many filmmakers who dreamed, imagined and worked so that their message and their aesthetic would reach an audience ever more enthralled by the seventh art and the rich history it holds.

references.description: The Story of Film: An Odyssey is an epic journey through the history of cinema. Guided by film historian Mark Cousins, this 15-part love letter to the movies spans from the invention of film in the 19th century to the digital industry of the 21st.

references.description: As the title itself says, it revisits the ten years since the release of City of God (2002), the feature by Fernando Meirelles and Kátia Lund that received four Oscar nominations. references.title: Lessons from the Screenplay
references.subtitle: English-language YouTube channel
references.description:
I believe that a more informed audience raises the bar for storytelling. That examining the techniques used to tell great stories makes your own writing better and your appreciation for the stories deeper.

With Lessons from the Screenplay, I make videos that analyze movie scripts to examine exactly how and why they are so good at telling their stories. Part educational series and part love letter to awesome films, Lessons from the Screenplay aims to be a fun way to learn more about your favorite films and help us all become better storytellers.

I’ll be releasing new videos every couple weeks, and taking suggestions about what scripts I should look at in future episodes.
